title: Is there a white style and a black style
summary: Rose says styles differ, but Perrin's and Fletcher Henderson's early orchestras, or Edmond Hall and Raymond Burke, can't be told apart by race. He concedes the Chicago style was largely white.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand
